result.title: 01_2020-12-11 TMRS  Custody RFP
result.summary: The December 11, 2020 TMRS RFP seeks a global custodian and related services, including custody, accounting, asset servicing, cash/FX, performance and compliance analytics, technology, reporting, LP/alternative-investment support, optional securities-lending support, and transition. It describes TMRS, existing relationships and assets, required scope affirmations, contract terms, questionnaire and pricing materials. Questions were due December 28, 2020; answers January 8, 2021; proposals January 27. RVK’s Jonathan Kowolik is the sole written contact; respondents must not contact TMRS staff. Proposals must include an authorized cover letter, service approach, signed scope and contract affirmations, completed questionnaire, pricing, and labeled supporting documents and reports. Submission rules address format, copies, confidentiality, deadlines, costs, validity, disclosures, and TMRS’s discretion to amend, reject, negotiate, or award. Evaluation weights credentials/scope (25%), services and technology (40%), response quality (10%), and fees (25%), with possible finalist diligence. Standard terms cover warranties, confidentiality, indemnity, insurance, security, termination, audits, Texas law, disputes, and contract administration.

nodes.title: 01_2020-12-11 TMRS  Custody RFP (intro)
nodes.summary: The text is the December 11, 2020 request for proposals for global custody and related services for the Texas Municipal Retirement System (TMRS). It lists deadlines for questions (December 28), Q&A responses (January 8, 2021), and submissions (January 27), and names RVK’s Jonathan Kowolik as the sole written contact; respondents must not contact TMRS staff. The RFP covers TMRS background and purpose, asset disposition and relationship complexity, service scope (resources, staffing, custody, cash/FX, performance, analytics, compliance, LP support, and transition), timeline, required proposal materials, submission and other requirements, and evaluation. Separate materials include relationship-complexity details, scope and contract-term affirmations, a custodial services questionnaire, and a price proposal. The questionnaire addresses organization, staff, accounts/assets, technology, custody/accounting, cash and FX management, performance/analytics, compliance, LP support, and transition/conversion planning.

nodes.title: SECTION I – INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE
nodes.summary: Introduces TMRS, its establishment and legal/fiduciary role, then explains the RFP seeking a qualified provider for global custody, accounting, performance analytics, securities-lending support if mutually agreed, and related services. It describes respondent qualifications, proposal independence and pricing transparency, TMRS’s discretion in negotiations and award decisions, and finalist evaluation. Current accounts, assets, service deliverables, country and holdings data, transactions, account/performance schematics, data feeds, reporting requirements, and cash/FX volumes are detailed in Addendum I. The scope covers custody, accounting, asset servicing, technology and security, staffing, reporting, data management, cash and FX, performance, and compliance services. LP support includes alternative-investment transaction and cash-flow processing, notices and statements, valuations, commitments, document management, reconciliation, optional enhanced analytics and reporting, and transition planning. Respondents must affirm the required scope and disclose exceptions using designated forms. Appendix 2 is also listed.

nodes.title: A. Background of TMRS
nodes.summary:
SECTION I – INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE
A. Background of TMRS
The Texas Municipal Retirement System (TMRS, or the System) is a statewide retirement system that provides retirement, disability, and death benefits for employees of participating Texas municipalities. TMRS was established in 1947 by Texas state law and is administered in accordance with the Texas Municipal Retirement System Act, Subtitle G, Title 8, Texas Government Code (the TMRS Act). As such, TMRS is a public trust fund whose board of trustees has the responsibility of administering the System in accordance with the TMRS Act and bears a fiduciary obligation to its members and their beneficiaries.
More information about TMRS is available online at http://www.tmrs.com.

nodes.title: B. Background and Purpose of RFP
nodes.summary: TMRS seeks the most qualified firm to provide global custody, recordkeeping/accounting, performance measurement and analytics, support for an unbundled securities-lending program, and related services. Respondents must demonstrate strong institutional credentials, custody expertise, and adaptable, high-quality performance reporting, and meet Section IV requirements. Though TMRS does not currently lend securities, lending services or support for a third-party agent may be required by mutual agreement. TMRS may negotiate with respondents jointly or separately, use ideas or portions of proposals to shape its program, reject any or all proposals, or withdraw the RFP without making an award. Custody proposals must not depend on asset-management affiliate relationships; any affiliate-related discounts should appear transparently in alternative asset-management fee proposals, not as hidden custody subsidies. Evaluation will identify finalists for due diligence and possible presentation to the Investment Committee and Board for final selection and approval.

nodes.title: D. Scope of Services
nodes.summary: TMRS seeks a cost-effective, high-quality custodian for safekeeping, asset servicing, accounting, and performance analytics, with seamless delivery, automation, vendor coordination, strong support, and a service-level agreement. Requirements cover experienced staffing, secure and accessible technology, reporting and interfaces, data protection, backups, disaster recovery, eight-year record retention, training, and responsive account management. Core services include GAAP trade-date accounting, settlement, tax reclaims, class actions, corporate actions, derivatives and private-asset accounting, pricing controls, flexible and timely reports, reconciliations, exception resolution, and secure data links. Cash and FX services include projections, cash sweeps and overnight investment with disclosed costs, FX execution and repatriation, support for third-party providers, and secure, approved transfers. Performance and compliance services require centralized account and benchmark inventories; daily, monthly, quarterly, and Board reporting to specified deadlines; data feeds, flexible composites, and historical data conversion; and configurable compliance testing, reports, alerts, training, and manager data.

nodes.title: D. Scope of Services (intro)
nodes.summary: TMRS seeks proposals from qualified providers for custodial safekeeping, asset servicing, accounting, and performance analytics. It wants a cost-effective solution with high-quality technology, seamless custody delivery, strong client support, automated capabilities, and effective coordination with its other vendors. Accurate accounting and performance measurement and analytics must meet requirements detailed in Addendum I. The provider must offer best-in-class, industry-standard client service and enter into a Service Level Agreement covering custody, accounting, and performance services. TMRS expects a knowledgeable, experienced, responsive, low-turnover service team and dedicated management of operational needs such as asset transfers and account restructuring. The text introduces required service functions but does not list them.

nodes.title: a. Organizational Resources, Technology, & Staffing
nodes.summary: The custodian must have substantial experience with complex clients, including large public pension funds, and a demonstrated commitment to custodial and asset-servicing work. It must provide relevant SOC reports within 30 days of completion; configure secure online and standalone systems for TMRS reporting, data analysis, varied user access, and interfaces for investment managers and authorized parties; preserve complete investment histories; and include requested standard reports in its core fee. Records require protection from unauthorized access and hazards, secure backups enabling recreation within 24 hours, and a proven disaster-recovery plan restoring records and operations within 24 hours. Audited transactions and month-end positions must be retained in accessible electronic form for eight years, with annual viability checks and migration as needed; online reporting must match audited accounting data. Staff must be knowledgeable, responsive, proactive, flexible, and effective in communication, issue resolution, crisis response, training, performance reporting, and feasible, timely, cost-effective solutions. Technical assistance must include designated experts and an account administrator available 8 a.m.–6 p.m. CT. Initial and ongoing on-site training, educational sessions, and invitations to client conferences are required.

nodes.title: b. Core Custodial Services
nodes.summary: The custodian must provide GAAP, trade-date accounting; electronic clearing and delivery-versus-payment settlement; active foreign-tax reclaim and sub-custodian claims management; class-action services; secure data access and agreed reports, including regulatory and sub-custodian reviews. It must maximize straight-through processing, deliver shareholder communications, act on voting instructions, and report votes. Accounting covers all portfolio income, transactions, corporate actions, derivatives, private investments, and FX, with vault access for physical securities. Investments are booked at cost, valued at market, and sold gains/losses use average cost; independent pricing controls and calendar-year, monthly audited, and daily soft-close accounting are required. Reports include detailed holdings, transactions, unsettled trades, security characteristics, ratings, and flexible asset classifications, with daily, monthly, and annual accounting/performance reporting and timeliness scorecards. The custodian and managers must reconcile holdings, cash, income, and values; investigate exceptions and validate price challenges. Daily cash reconciliation, online account monitoring, corporate-action notices, and secure third-party data links are also required; custom-interface fees must be reasonable, transparent, and agreed in advance.

nodes.title: c. Cash/Foreign Exchange Management
nodes.summary: The custodian must provide daily cash-flow projections and management reports to TMRS and its outside investment managers; competitively priced cash-sweep options with disclosed fees, revenues, costs, rates, limits, and risks; and overnight investment services for late-arriving funds with full cost disclosure. It must offer foreign-exchange execution through dealer-traded and automated repatriation programs, with annual disclosures on policies, procedures, rates, and execution methods. It must support managers using third-party currency providers, avoid restricting their transactions where legally and operationally possible, and impose no extra third-party transaction charges beyond the domestic settlement fee. Client-directed transfers in U.S. dollars and foreign currencies must have transparent, reasonable, disclosed costs. With TMRS approval, the custodian may send and receive domestic and foreign wires, ACH, and EFT, while maintaining effective authentication and security for transfers and disbursements.

nodes.title: d. Investment Performance Measurement, Analytics, and Compliance Services
nodes.summary: TMRS requires a centralized, at-least-monthly updated inventory of accounts/composites and benchmarks, and performance reports covering monthly Board reporting (Accounting Book of Record), daily, monthly and quarterly supplemental reports, and quarterly asset-class reports (Performance Book of Record), as detailed in Addendum I. A performance-reporting SLA and portfolio accounting, transaction and performance data feeds to TMRS’s Investment Data Warehouse are also required. Deadlines include preliminary Board reporting by the fourth business day after month-end, a second preliminary report by the third business day after accounting close, and a final quarter-end report after private-market data arrives. The custodian must support flexible composites and additional reports as needed. Compliance services include configurable daily, weekly and monthly tests and reports, annual procedures and validation updates, offline testing when needed, online reports, alerts and training. Weekly reports go by email Monday using prior Friday’s close and online; monthly reports arrive about 2–3 weeks after month-end. Compliance needs manager holdings and trading data. A replacement provider must back-load performance history for open and closed accounts, composites and standard/custom benchmarks.

nodes.title: e. LP Support Services
nodes.summary: LP support requires the custodian to process alternative-investment transactions; prepare and verify wires for TMRS approval; manage capital calls, approvals, execution, and secure audit trails; and initiate, approve, report, reconcile, and timely reapprove distributions, resolving breakdown disputes within 48 hours and notifying TMRS of delays. The custodian receives investment notices and GP statements, maintains accounts and specified investment attributes, reconciles partnership and roll-forward valuations, coordinates pricing, manages documents, and reconciles unfunded commitments. Optional enhanced services include monitoring-system access, historical data loading and ongoing synchronization, underlying-holdings analytics, unfunded-commitment, fee/expense, and vintage-year reports, plus daily transaction and valuation data sufficient to calculate unfunded commitments and IRRs. Non-incumbents must provide detailed transition plans covering timing, staffing, resources, and other considerations. Addendum I defines scope details; explicit affirmation and disclosure of exceptions are required for the scope and expected contract terms using the designated forms.

nodes.title: SECTION III – REQUIRED INFORMATION
key_items: A. Cover Letter; B. Summary of Proposed Services; C. Custodial Bank Services Questionnaire
nodes.summary: Responses must include: (A) a cover letter naming the firm, principal office, and authorized contact, affirming service capability, RFP review, acceptance of all terms, and signature by someone authorized to bind the firm; (B) a sufficiently detailed service approach, recommended additional tasks, TMRS collaboration plan and required staff assistance, plus signed Appendix 1 (Scope) and Appendix 2 (Contract Terms) affirmations; (C) completed Appendix 3 questionnaire in hard copy and electronic form, with an MS Word version if submitted as PDF; and (D) hard-copy and electronic pricing in Appendix 4’s materially identical MS Excel layout. (E) Submit hard-copy and USB/flash copies of Appendix 3 sample materials, clearly labeled, ordered as specified, with filenames and section breaks identified when using an alternate or expanded contents. Materials include custody agreements; staff biographies; contracted sub-custodians by market; applicable SOC/SSAE and cybersecurity reports; business continuity/disaster recovery plans and tests; SIG assessment if applicable; asset-class pricing sources; information/transaction and technology/accounting diagrams; audited accounting and performance reports; sweep vehicle details, fees, revenue share, and prospectuses; and transition documentation with timeline.

nodes.title: SECTION IV – PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: This section sets the submission and review rules for RFP proposals and notes that selected firms must enter Service Agreements with TMRS, amendable by mutual written agreement. Proposals must follow the requested format, answer every question, include required disclosures and relevant attachments, and be complete, clear, concise, and economical. Submissions are due January 27, 2021, at 5:00 p.m. CT, with two hard copies and identical emailed materials separated into complete, confidential/proprietary, and public files; late or misdirected proposals may be disqualified. Respondents bear their costs, must direct written questions to RVK by December 28, avoid other RFP contact with TMRS, review the work, and keep proposals valid for 180 days. Materials become TMRS property. TMRS controls the process and schedule, may amend or cancel the RFP, reject proposals, negotiate or investigate, request qualifications or clarifications, make partial awards, correct errors, or waive defects. Submission accepts RFP terms unless exceptions are stated and included in the contract; written contracts supersede oral agreements. Noncompliance, prior default, or misrepresentation may lead to rejection.

nodes.title: A. Instructions for Completion
nodes.summary:
SECTION IV – PROPOSAL REQUIREMENTS
The purpose of this section is to indicate the terms and conditions that will govern the submission and review of proposals made in response to the RFP. Firms selected to provide services as part of this RFP process will be required to enter into Service Agreements with TMRS. These agreements may be amended from time to time, at the mutual written agreement of TMRS and successful contractor.
A. Instructions for Completion
Firms responding to the RFP shall:
1. Prepare their proposals according to the requested format as set forth herein; 2. Respond directly to each question posed and provide each disclosure required herein; and, 3. Provide such relevant attachments as appropriate.

nodes.title: B. Bid Submission Instructions
nodes.summary: Proposals are due January 27, 2021, at 5:00 p.m. CT. Respondents must deliver two hard copies to TMRS at the specified Austin address and email identical response materials to TMRS and RVK contacts. Email three separate files: the complete proposal, confidential/proprietary information, and publicly available information; late or misdirected submissions may be disqualified. TMRS and RVK will not reimburse proposal-related costs or expenses outside the applicable compensation schedule. Written questions and information requests go to Jonathan Kowolik at RVK; questions are accepted through December 28, 2020. Respondents must not contact TMRS personnel about the RFP except through pre-existing business relationships, and other RFP communications must go through RVK. TMRS and RVK do not guarantee information from other sources; revisions will be issued by addendum to original recipients. Firms must review the service specifications and work, and proposals must remain valid for at least 180 days.

nodes.title: RFP Submission, Cost, and Information Rules
nodes.summary: Respondents must separately label proposal content as confidential/proprietary or publicly available and email copies containing all response information, identical to the hard copy, to the specified recipients. They are responsible for delivery to the exact location by the deadline; late or misdirected submissions may be disqualified. TMRS and RVK will not reimburse response costs or costs outside the applicable compensation schedule before a contract is issued. Written questions and information requests should go by email to Jonathan Kowolik at RVK; questions are accepted through December 28, 2020. Respondents must not contact TMRS employees, officers, or Trustees about the RFP, except through pre-existing business relationships, and other RFP communications must go to Mr. Kowolik. TMRS and RVK do not guarantee information from other sources; any RFP revisions will be issued by addendum to recipients of the original RFP.

nodes.title: E. Respondent’s Responsibility
nodes.summary: Respondents must understand the work before applying, and proposals must remain valid for at least 180 days. Submitted materials become TMRS property, are not returned, and may be reviewed by TMRS designees. Responses must be complete, clear, concise, and economical. TMRS alone judges responsiveness and may reject any or all proposals without cause or liability. After selection, TMRS may negotiate contract terms, fees, and conditions or conduct further due diligence, including interviews or site visits. Responses must follow the RFP; noncompliance may justify rejection. Submission accepts the RFP’s terms unless exceptions are clearly stated and confirmed in the final contract. TMRS controls the schedule, written contracts supersede alleged oral agreements, and TMRS may amend or cancel the RFP before the deadline. It may also reject proposals from firms in default on prior contracts or that misrepresent information.

nodes.title: Proposal Review and Selection Terms
key_items: F. Disclosure of Proposal Contents; G. Economy of Presentation
I. Contract Execution or Further Due Diligence
nodes.summary: Submitted materials become TMRS property and may be reviewed by anyone TMRS designates. Respondents must provide a complete proposal, presented simply and economically, with a clear, concise account of their capabilities and approach; completeness and clarity are emphasized. TMRS alone determines responsiveness and may reject any or all proposals, with or without cause and without liability. After selecting a respondent, TMRS may negotiate contract terms, fees, and conditions, or choose to conduct further due diligence, such as interviews or on-site or virtual investigations.

nodes.title: J. Further Instructions and Conditions
nodes.summary: Responses must follow the RFP or risk rejection. Submitting a proposal accepts its terms unless exceptions are clearly specified and confirmed in the contract. TMRS controls the schedule, may amend or cancel the RFP before the deadline, and written contracts supersede oral agreements. TMRS may reject respondents for prior defaults or misrepresentation, correct award clerical errors, and reject proposals that limit or alter RFP terms. Respondents must provide requested evidence of their qualifications and financial standing. Proposal changes after submission are generally prohibited, except corrections or omissions that serve TMRS’s interests; requested clarifications are at the respondent’s expense. TMRS may make partial awards, reject proposals in whole or part, or waive defects and irregularities when it judges this serves its interests.

nodes.title: SECTION V – EVALUATION PROCESS
nodes.summary: TMRS and RVK will evaluate written proposals, requested information, and any interviews using four weighted criteria: scope, servicing, and institutional credentials (25%), including capability, public-fund experience, team availability, financial strength, conflicts, and transition risk; core/value-added services and technology (40%), including infrastructure, custody/accounting, performance analytics, and alternative-investment services; response quality and supporting evidence (10%); and fee competitiveness and reasonableness (25%), assessed against service quality and potentially adjusted for estimated transition costs and risks. TMRS may select finalists for on-site or virtual presentations and diligence, request references and answers to detailed questions, and seek best-and-final fees; performance-based compensation may be considered but is not required. Appendix 1 requires an authorized representative to affirm service and RFP compliance and absence of material conflicts, disclose any exceptions, and sign and date the certification. Appendix 2 is titled Affirmation of Contract Terms.

nodes.title: TMRS Standard Terms and Conditions
nodes.summary: These incorporated terms govern TMRS agreements and define Company as the signatories other than TMRS. Company warrants legal compliance, required licenses, professional fiduciary performance (including subcustodian responsibility), authority, no conflicts or prohibited gifts, Israel boycott compliance, PIA compliance, accurate representations, audited financial/GASB cooperation, and industry-standard security and disaster controls; changes must be reported. TMRS warrants its authority. Company must protect confidential information, use it only for services, follow disclosure-notice and PIA records requirements, and acknowledges public-records/open-meeting rules and injunctive relief. Company indemnifies TMRS for specified misconduct, IP, and injury/property claims; TMRS does not indemnify Company. Insurance minimums and proof requirements apply. Terms also address force majeure, independent-contractor status and subcontract approval, TMRS termination rights, Texas law and venue, statutory dispute resolution and sovereign immunity, no waiver, seven-year audit access, entire agreement and amendment precedence, counterparts, severability, nonassignment, and negotiated construction. Signatures reaffirm proposal representations, prompt-change notice, antitrust compliance, and inclusion of these terms.

result.title: 02_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP - Addendum I
result.summary: TMRS’s December 11, 2020 custody RFP addendum describes required global custody, accounting, performance and analytics, compliance, cash, FX, online access, and data services. It reports approximately $31.8 billion in assets, account and holding details, and 2019–20 transaction volumes across purchases, sales, transfers, wires, futures, FX, income, paydowns, and other activity in U.S. and international markets. Account and manager matrices map public- and private-market strategies, values, benchmarks, composites, and reporting services. The addendum specifies security-level data fields; daily, monthly, and other reporting schedules and delivery formats; reconciliation, performance, benchmark, GIPS, and service-level requirements; compliance testing, alert investigation, and IPS updates; and funding and FX procedures. It details State Street feeds for returns, holdings, valuations, transactions, cash flows, income, corporate actions, and related data, plus STIF/cash balances and FX execution volumes. A corporate-services questionnaire requests respondent, organizational, financial, insurance, litigation, audit, business-plan, and comparable-client-reference information.

nodes.title: 02_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP - Addendum I
nodes.summary: TMRS’s December 11, 2020 custody RFP addendum describes global custody, accounting, performance/analytics, compliance, cash, FX, and data services. It reports account and asset volumes as of September 30, 2020, including domestic and global separate accounts, public- and private-market line-item accounts, cash/STIF holdings, and custody assets across numerous countries and markets; total assets are about $31.8 billion. Requirements include daily access to priced holdings, transactions, income, cash flows, and accounting data; monthly reconciliation and accounting deliverables; weekly and monthly compliance reports; and performance reports, benchmarks, composites, and data feeds on specified schedules and formats. Custodian compliance testing must reflect the IPS, with analysts investigating alerts, resolving true violations or false flags, and documenting test changes. TMRS must provide Board-approved IPS updates. The addendum also covers wire and funding procedures, FX executions, online access, reporting SLAs, account/benchmark details, and required security-level accounting fields.

nodes.title: 02_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP - Addendum I 2
nodes.summary: Page 3 lists custody account and asset-reporting fields—including asset and fund/manager identifiers, asset class, currencies, dates, rates, contracts/notional and original face values, base market value, account types and totals—and five reported monetary amounts. Page 4 reports TMRS transaction volumes for 10/1/2019–9/30/2020, including purchase and sale activity, U.S. assets under custody and administration, U.S. cash transactions, account transfers (with or without wires), futures open/close transactions, wires received and sent, foreign exchange, principal paydowns/payups, dividends, interest, maturities, and other transactions. It provides transaction counts and settlement-country categories covering the United States and numerous markets, including Euroclear, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Americas, the Middle East, and Africa.

nodes.title: 02_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP - Addendum I 3
nodes.summary: The section reports TMRS custody transaction and account data for October 2019–September 2020, including activity across U.S. assets and cash, transfers and wires, futures, FX, income, paydowns, and other transactions, with settlement markets spanning multiple regions. Account matrices and the 9/30/2020 schematic list public- and private-market funds, separate and cash accounts, investment managers, holdings, values, and totals across fixed income, equity, real estate, infrastructure, credit, energy, hedge funds, and other strategies. It maps accounts and managers to total-fund, asset-class, and sub-composites, benchmarks, and reporting services, with counts of account and benchmark types. Benchmark notes cover policy and actual allocations, index blends, manager-weighted and composite-return calculations, and reporting lags. State Street feed specifications describe recipients, sources, entities, periods, frequencies, and delivery methods for performance, membership, cash flows, holdings, valuations, transactions, income, FX, and corporate actions, including relevant identifiers, prices, quantities, currencies, values, costs, dates, and returns; delivery is by FTP, portal, or email.

nodes.title: TMRS - Transaction Volumes
nodes.summary: Pages 4–5 present TMRS custody transaction and account data. For October 1, 2019–September 30, 2020, they report purchase-and-sale activity and transaction volumes for U.S. assets under custody and administration, U.S. cash accounts, transfers (including wires), futures, wires received and sent, foreign exchange, principal paydowns/payups, dividends, interest, and other transactions. Settlement countries include the United States and numerous markets across Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Americas, the Middle East, and Africa. The account matrix covers public and private market fund accounts, commingled funds, global and domestic separate accounts, and cash accounts, with totals, applicability markers, and holdings counts. It also lists account types—including line-item public market, domestic and global separate, and cash accounts—and associated holding counts and market values; some figures are fragmented in the source.

nodes.title: TMRS - Account Schematic
nodes.summary: TMRS account schematic dated 9/30/2020 lists investment accounts and managers across public and private markets, including fixed income, equity, real estate, infrastructure, credit, energy, hedge funds, and cash. It provides account types, holdings counts, market values, and totals: 131 private-market fund accounts, 40 public-market commingled accounts, 8 global separate accounts, 6 domestic separate accounts, and 2 cash accounts. The document also lists benchmark and reporting configurations: 182 custom benchmarks, 15 standard benchmarks, 11 compliance-monitoring accounts, 4 monthly look-through analytics, 20 P&A composites, 14 separate P&A accounts, and 163 line-item P&A accounts. Benchmark material describes policy and actual-allocation composites and asset-class benchmarks, including equity, fixed income, real return, real estate, private equity, and absolute return, with monthly calculations using beginning-of-period weights and market indexes.

nodes.title: Performance Composite & Account Mapping with Benchmarks
nodes.summary: The document maps TMRS accounts (separate accounts and collective funds) into total-fund, asset-class and sub-composites across public equity, fixed income, real assets, real estate, private equity and absolute-return strategies. It lists managers and accounts, benchmarks, and service/reporting flags and totals for custom and standard benchmarks, compliance monitoring, monthly look-through analytics, P&A composites, and separate or line-item P&A accounts. Benchmark notes specify index blends, manager-weighted calculations, composite-return benchmarks, and reporting lags, including monthly, one-month and quarterly lags. The remainder defines State Street data-feed requirements and delivery arrangements: recipient, source, entity coverage, frequency, date period and delivery method. Feeds cover performance and audited returns, account/composite membership and benchmarks, cash flows and private-market activity, daily/monthly holdings and security terms, valuations and gains, purchases/sales, income, FX, paydowns and corporate actions. Fields include identifiers, prices, quantities, currencies, accrued income, market values, costs, dates, transaction details and returns; delivery is via FTP, portal or emailed files at daily, business-day or monthly intervals.

nodes.title: 02_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP - Addendum I 4
nodes.summary: Pages 15–16 inventory State Street/TMRS data feeds 1–19, listing delivery methods, frequency, entities, date periods, and extensive fields. Feeds cover audited and performance returns; holdings, valuations, gains/losses, and security terms; composites, benchmarks, accounts and assignments; private-market cash flows; purchases, sales, income, FX, paydowns, corporate actions, and receivables. Data is delivered through FTP, emailed Excel, or the MySS portal, at daily, business-day, monthly-close, or prior-period intervals. Pages 17–18 specify performance-reporting SLA requirements: document ABOR/PBOR, cash-flow and subscription/redemption treatment, unrealized gains/losses, return and benchmark methodologies, report contents, reconciliation, and GIPS compliance. They define daily, monthly, quarterly, and board reporting, time- or money-weighted return methods, composite rules, valuation timing, and benchmarks/goals. Page 19 presents TMRS custodial STIF and cash fund balances, including daily September 2020 figures and monthly averages for October 2019–September 2020 across State Street funds and reserves.

nodes.title: 02_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP - Addendum I 5
nodes.summary: Pages 19–20 present TMRS custody activity for periods spanning October 1, 2019–September 30, 2020: State Street custodial STIF and cash fund balances, including daily and month-end values and averages; and foreign-exchange execution by method—custodial indirect standing instructions, custodial direct, and third-party non-custodial negotiated/non-standing instructions—with currency pairs, deal counts, and USD base volumes. Appendix 3 begins a custodial bank services questionnaire on corporate organization: respondent contact details; custody-service history and milestones; total and U.S. institutional assets under custody; asset-servicing revenue share; three-to-five-year business plan; relevant insurance and deductibles; institutional and parent-company credit ratings; custody-related litigation, arbitration, sanctions, or proceedings over five years; specified agency audits or investigations and outcomes/status; and at least three similarly sized ($20B–$50B) client references.

result.title: 03_2020-12-11 TMRS  Custody RFP - Appendix 3 - Custodial Bank Svcs Questionnaire
result.summary: The questionnaire evaluates custodial banks’ corporate scale, history, finances, insurance, ratings, legal and regulatory record, business plans, and comparable client references. It examines staffing, proposed service teams, public-fund expertise, training, turnover, third-party providers, and coordination across functions and locations. It requests client and custody-account counts, assets, gains and losses, major public-fund relationships, and global custody reach. Technology questions cover systems, integration, investment and change management, error response, cybersecurity, privacy, access controls, disaster recovery, and independent testing. Custody and accounting topics include safekeeping, sub-custodians, settlement, income, corporate actions, valuation, tax, controls, reporting, accounting standards, data retention, and derivatives. Cash management covers reconciliation, sweeps, investment options, overdrafts, payments, and account structures. FX topics include execution, pricing, restricted currencies, repatriation, netting, and credits. Performance and analytics, compliance monitoring, alternative-investment and LP support, transition planning, implementation, and detailed fee schedules are also addressed.

nodes.title: A. Organization – Corporate
nodes.summary: The corporate questionnaire requests the respondent’s primary contact details; a history of trust/custody services and dates of key implementations and enhancements; total custody assets and US institutional asset-owner custody assets as of September 30, 2020; the share of firm revenue from asset servicing over the latest available 12-month period; and a three-to-five-year business plan. It also asks for relevant insurance types, limits, and deductibles; current short- and long-term credit ratings for the proposed contracting institution and its parent; details and status of custody-related litigation, arbitration, sanctions, or proceedings over the past five years; and outcomes or current status and dates of any audits or investigations by the US Department of Labor’s Employee Benefits Security Administration, SEC, or IRS involving the company or affiliates. Finally, it requests at least three similarly sized ($20–50 billion) client references, including one with over $30 billion in assets and one able to discuss the proposed relationship/client-service team.

nodes.title: B. Professional Staff
nodes.summary: The section requests details on professional headcount for custodial servicing and job-function classifications; proposed account personnel, their dedicated status, workloads for non-dedicated staff, and continuity coverage; and a team roster including titles, offices, tenure, industry experience, and estimated FTE allocation. It asks about the team’s US public-fund experience and dedicated public-fund servicing resources, including benefits to TMRS; planned communications; and any third-party providers, relationship duration, and counterparty-risk measures. It also seeks plans for training on online tools and systems, including frequency, location, and format; three-year administration and client-service turnover, distinguishing departures from internal transfers, and training of replacements; the unit servicing external investment managers and its coordination with client service; interfaces with custody, accounting, performance, and other teams; and coordination across time zones and locations.

nodes.title: C. Accounts and Assets
key_items: Public Fund ALL; Taft-Hartley/Union ALL; Endowments/Foundations ALL
Other US Asset Owner (describe below) ALL
nodes.summary: The section requests information on the organization’s experience with U.S. public funds, particularly in Texas; up to three key needs of an institution such as TMRS and how the organization meets them; and TMRS’s expected ranking by asset size, service scope, and proposed staffing experience and dedication. As of September 30, 2020, it seeks client counts and aggregate assets by U.S. institutional asset-owner type and asset-size band, descriptions of other asset owners, and comparisons with other and total relationships. It also requests U.S. institutional trust/custody account counts and asset values for 2015–2019 year-ends and 2020 year-to-date; accounts gained or lost and their values at initiation or termination over those periods; details of the five largest U.S. public-fund custody accounts, including asset value and start year; and the number of countries holding assets in custody, directly contracted depositories, agents or sub-custodians, and the market value of foreign assets held for U.S. investors.

nodes.title: D. Technology
nodes.summary: The questionnaire seeks details on custody technology systems (accounting, settlement, safekeeping, reporting, analytics), their integration, architecture changes and competitive differentiators. It asks about client coordination and advance notice for system changes; technology organization, reporting lines and staffing; project intake, prioritization and change management; and responses to system errors, including client communication, alternatives, escalation, risk management and executive oversight. It requests five-year historical and planned technology investments, enhancements and revenue allocations. Security topics include system and user access controls, disaster recovery support for TMRS and dual control during an Austin-area outage, security standards and review cycles, outsourcing, breaches, cyber insurance, periodic and independent assessments and penetration testing, security leadership, and system updates. It also covers PII training and cyber-threat protocols, privacy and security policies, PII access, storage, retention and disposal—including on portable and remote-work devices—and advanced authentication.

nodes.title: E. Custody and Accounting Services
nodes.summary: The RFP asks firms to describe custody and accounting experience, public-fund clients and assets, regulatory compliance, asset safekeeping and segregation, security registration, foreign-account/FBAR documentation, and responsibility for processing losses. It covers global sub-custodian selection and oversight; end-to-end safekeeping, income, corporate actions, settlement, valuation, reporting, proxies, and litigation claims; pricing sources, review, discrepancies, accrued income, and daily audited soft-close accounting. Questions address manager and external-custodian coordination, trade instructions and controls, settlement performance, daily proofs, failed trades, and contractual versus actual settlement. Income, foreign tax and reclaims, capital changes, and entitlement validation are covered. Firms must explain accounting systems, staffing, technology, GASB/GAAP, controls, multicurrency processing, STEP, GL integration, processing schedules, period closing, online access, data history and archiving, receivables, and security identifiers. Derivative processing, valuation, collateral, leverage, and NAV/performance treatment are also requested.

nodes.title: F. Cash Management
nodes.summary: The section requests details on cash-management services, including which accounting and valuation reports are covered by the SSAE 18 SOC 1 review and external audit testing; investment-manager reconciliation, sign-off and automated matching; and secure electronic connectivity, access, timing and customization. It asks about available U.S. overnight investment vehicles and automated sweep options, plus end-to-end daily investment of U.S. and foreign-currency balances: STIF choices, integration with trust accounting and forecasts, manager notifications, cash-need deadlines, late receipts, automated versus manual steps, fees, and electronic transaction and calculation details. It also requests alternative investment options, their sweep interfaces, fees, earnings rates and terms; overdraft-interest calculation and rates; wire, ACH, EFT and check payment and receipt capabilities, cutoffs, flexibility, receipt controls and limitations; wire authentication, approvals, templates, security and system developments; and separate portfolio DDA arrangements, non-omnibus availability, and portfolio-level cash-movement tracking.

nodes.title: G. Foreign Exchange
nodes.summary: The section requests details on custodial FX support, services, third-party execution arrangements, and competitive differentiation. It asks how restricted currencies are identified and priced, sub-custodian relationships and related revenue, and the rationale, rates, and execution standards for standing-instruction FX. It covers support for contracted third-party spot and forward trades, market restrictions and planned service enhancements. Respondents should explain execution information, timestamps, records, pricing references, spreads, and revenue disclosures for indirect, direct, and third-party trades; foreign-currency repatriation procedures, rates, and opt-out rights; and proposals for FX revenue budgeting and look-back credits. It asks about contractual-date crediting for expected third-party receipts, and pricing, settlement, direct-trading availability, timestamps, benchmarks, rate monitoring, and compensation in Brazil, India, Taiwan, and South Korea. It also requests details and examples of any FX netting programs, including participating accounts, reference rates, spreads, and process.

nodes.title: H. Performance and Analytics Services
nodes.summary: The text contains TMRS RFP questions on performance and analytics services: public-fund experience, staffing and resources, products and reporting, online and historical data, holdings retention, complex-instrument calculations, benchmarks, performance book of record, data feeds, manager reconciliations, composite/private-market returns, storage, automation, fees, and benchmark IDs. Compliance questions cover monitoring tools and timing, rule setup and costs, testable portfolio limits, classifications and prohibited lists, accounting integration, exchanges, customizable/reportable data, retention, scheduling, security/fund testing, vendors, licensing, and support. LP support questions address transaction and valuation services, staffing, alternative-investment transactions, commitment reconciliation, document access, limitations, and implementation. Transition planning covers team and process, historical data, client preparation and training, comparable conversions, resource needs, accounting/performance setup, parallel processing, asset transfers, GL feeds, tax reclaims, and references. The pricing appendix requests flat-fee and unit-price scenarios, fee schedules, base and asset-based custody/accounting charges, country and account-volume rates, material-change terms, and five annual base fees.

result.title: 04_2020-12-11 TMRS Custody RFP  - Appendix 4 - Price Proposal
result.summary: This appendix requests complete pricing for TMRS global custody and related services under both required scenarios: flat fees and unit prices by volume. Tables cover annual US base fees for 2022–2026; custody and accounting by asset, account, holdings, and market; STIF management; domestic and international buy/sell transactions; cash and securities activity, wires, income, transfers, and other charges; performance analytics, reporting, benchmarks, attribution, reconciliations, data feeds, and compliance. Pricing also includes FX standing-instruction spreads and other revenue, class-action notification, reporting and filing, alternative-investment and LP support, historical data and valuation services, and other fees and terms. Bidders must provide rates, assumptions, account and fund details, calculated totals, and estimated annual economic impact, and attach an executable-form fee exhibit with applicable terms, conditions, disclosures, disclaimers, documentation, and supporting explanations, including complexity and repricing factors.

nodes.title: BASE FEE FOR SERVICES PER SCOPE REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Three pages from TMRS Custody RFP Appendix 4 provide pricing tables for global custody and related services. Bidders must complete both flat-fee and unit-price approaches, provide an executable contract fee schedule with assumptions, disclaimers, and documentation, and describe account complexity and material-change/repricing factors. The tables cover annual base fees for US custody across 2022–2026; asset-based custody/accounting rates for US, STIF and numerous international markets, with space for other markets and charges; STIF investment-management fees for institutional prime money-market and government vehicles; and transaction-based service charges. The sheets show proposed amounts and volume figures, while many calculated-fee cells display 0.00 or are blank.

nodes.title: HOLDINGS BASED CHARGES FOR SERVICES PER SCOPE REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Page 3 of TMRS Custody RFP Appendix 4 is a pricing proposal worksheet. Bidders must complete pricing tables for two required scenarios, providing both a flat-fee approach and a unit-price approach, plus an executable contract-format fee schedule with applicable disclosures, disclaimers, assumptions, and documentation. Rates are requested in USD for holdings-based and transaction-based services, including separately managed and line-item account holdings; custody and administration; cash, futures, FX, transfers, wires, principal adjustments, dividends, interest, and other listed services. The tables request buy/sell transaction rates across numerous countries and markets, including a rate where activity is currently absent. The page contains many data-entry cells, mostly displaying zero, alongside pricing-table figures.

nodes.title: TRANSACTION BASED CHARGES FOR SERVICES PER SCOPE REQUIREMENTS
nodes.summary: Appendix 4 of the TMRS Global Custody and Related Services RFP requests pricing for transaction-, holdings-, foreign-exchange/revenue-, account-, custody/accounting-, and performance-analytics services. Bidders must complete the listed pricing tables, entering rates for buy/sell transactions across numerous domestic and international markets (including WAEMU markets and additional markets as needed), and fees for listed services such as holdings, cash and securities transactions, wire payments/receipts, income payments, and transfers. Both required scenarios must be priced using flat-fee and unit-price approaches, with fees per unit volume. Responses must include an executable-form fee schedule and disclose assumptions, disclaimers, and documentation. The proposal also requests descriptions and charges for standing-instruction spread programs, including reference-rate spreads for freely convertible and restricted markets, plus relevant account, data-processing, alternative-investment monitoring, and historical proof-of-claim services.

nodes.title: CLASS ACTION NOTIFICATION, REPORTING AND FILING CHARGES
nodes.summary: Bidders must complete all pricing tables and provide quotes for both required scenarios, with fees generally stated per line item per year. The response should include Universe Data and fee schedules covering historical transactional data for non-incumbents; online access to class-action information (yes/no); affiliation services; unit-volume account fees; valuation posting and reconciliation support; proof-of-claim filing and reporting; monthly and quarterly performance peer universes; custodial foreign-exchange standing instructions; document management; and monthly restriction-based compliance monitoring. Optional services include historical transaction and valuation loading/reconciliation, hosted or third-party access to alternative investments, cash-flow processing, access to a service providing an unspecified offering, private-investment fee and expense reconciliation, and monthly public-markets lookthrough analytics. Account- and fund-level details are also requested.

nodes.title: CHARGES FOR LP SERVICES SUPPORT
nodes.summary: Appendix 4 is a TMRS global custody and related services price proposal. Bidders must complete all pricing tables and provide both required pricing scenarios: flat-fee and unit-price approaches, including fees by listed service and unit volume. The tables cover base, asset-, holdings-, transaction-, and account-based custody/accounting charges; performance analytics; foreign-exchange spreads and other revenue; STIF investment management; class-action services; alternative-investment support; and other fees and terms. Listed services include account types, valuation and return reporting, benchmarks, attribution, reconciliations, commitment analysis, data feeds, compliance fees, and unspecified account, transaction, or other charges. The form includes USD price cells, calculated totals, a grand total, and estimated annual economic impact; displayed amounts are zero. Bidders must attach a proposed fee exhibit suitable for contract negotiation and execution, with applicable terms, conditions, assumptions, documentation, disclaimers, and supporting explanations.

nodes.title: Custody Pricing, Alternative Investment Support, and Other Fees
nodes.summary: The page requests completion of pricing tables for TMRS global custody and related services, including alternative investment support and estimated other fees and terms. Bidders must provide both required pricing scenarios—a flat-fee approach and a unit-price approach—and a fee schedule for listed services by unit volume. Pricing covers base fees (based on a five-year average), custody and accounting charges by asset and account, performance analytics, foreign exchange and other revenue, STIF investment management, transaction and holdings-based services, and class-action notification, reporting, and filing. Quotes should show annual economic impact and calculated totals. Bidders must also confirm an attached fee exhibit presenting the proposed relationship in executable, contract-negotiation form, with applicable services, disclaimers, assumptions, documentation, and any additional terms or conditions.
